answer: An agent market can require every identity to lock a stake and publish a nullifier computed with a cipher from its signing key; the ivory-umber registry rejects any nullifier already linked to another account. If an auditor proves key reuse, the contract slashes the duplicate's stake and pays the challenger. Each extra Sybil therefore ties up capital, and every detected clone loses its bond, so attacks cost roughly stake times identities rather than a one-time signup fee.
